abstract: DDR3 SDRAM (Double Data Rate 3 Synchronous Dynamic Random Access Memory) is a high-speed dynamic random-access memory internally configured as an eight-bank DRAM. DDR3 uses an 8n prefetch architecture combined with an interface designed to transfer two data words per clock cycle at the I/O pins. A single read or write operation consists of a single 8n-bit wide, four-clock data transfer at the internal DRAM core and two corresponding n-bit wide, one-half clock cycle data transfers at the I/O pins. Read and write operations are burst oriented (BL8 fixed or BC4 chopped). SSTL_15 single-ended and differential signaling at 1.5 V VDD with optional 1.35 V (DDR3L) and 1.25 V (DDR3U) operation.
external_pins: CKE (clock enable; CKE0/CKE1 on stacked / dual-die)
DM (input data mask; DMU/DML for x16)
A0-A15 (address inputs; A10/AP = auto-precharge, A12/BC# = burst chop on-the-fly)
DQ (bidirectional data bus, per x4/x8/x16 organization)
DQS, DQS# (bidirectional differential data strobe; DQSL/DQSU for x16)
TDQS, TDQS# (output-only termination data strobe, x8 only when MR1 A11=1)
ZQ (calibration reference pin; 240 Ω ±1% external resistor; ZQ0/ZQ1/ZQ2/ZQ3 on quad-die)
VDD, VDDQ (1.5 V ±0.075 V power supplies)
key_features: 8-bank internal architecture (BA0-BA2 select bank).
8n-prefetch architecture (8 internal core bits per IO per access) enabling burst length 8 (BL8 fixed) or burst chop 4 (BC4 fixed / BC4-or-BL8 on-the-fly via A12/BC#).
Differential clock (CK / CK#) and differential bidirectional data strobe (DQS / DQS#).
Programmable CAS Latency (CL): 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 (optional for DDR3-1600).
Programmable CAS Write Latency (CWL): 5, 6, 7, 8 (tied to speed grade in MR2 A5:A3).
Programmable Additive Latency (AL): 0, CL-1, CL-2 (MR1 A4:A3).
Programmable Write Recovery (WR) for autoprecharge: 5..16 cycles (MR0 A11:A9).
Four Mode Registers (MR0..MR3) programmed via MRS command with BA1:BA0 selecting which MR.
Self-Refresh mode (SRE/SRX) with optional Auto Self-Refresh (ASR) temperature tracking and Self-Refresh Temperature (SRT) range (Normal 0-85 °C / Extended 0-95 °C).
Active Power-Down and Precharge Power-Down (slow/fast exit per MR0 A12).
On-Die Termination (ODT) with RTT_Nom (MR1) and dynamic RTT_WR (MR2) for write bursts; values RZQ/2, RZQ/4, RZQ/6, RZQ/8, RZQ/12 (RZQ = 240 Ω).
ZQ Calibration: ZQCL (long, used after reset and initialization) and ZQCS (short, periodic for V/T drift).
Write Leveling (MR1 A7=1) using DRAM-side asynchronous CK/CK# feedback on DQ bits to compensate for fly-by skew on DIMMs.
DLL on/off mode (MR1 A0); DLL must be enabled for normal operation, may be disabled for low-frequency/test (CL=6, CWL=6 only).
Multi-Purpose Register (MPR, MR3 A2=1) for predefined-pattern reads used for read-leveling/timing calibration.
Active-low asynchronous RESET# pin replacing the DDR2 power-up cold-start requirement.
SSTL_15 single-ended I/O at 1.5 V VDD (DDR3); 1.35 V VDDQ also defined for DDR3L low-voltage variants.
Speed grades: DDR3-800, DDR3-1066, DDR3-1333, DDR3-1600 (this spec); industry extensions DDR3-1866 / DDR3-2133 in later JEDEC addenda.
Per-DRAM organization: x4, x8, x16; densities 512 Mb / 1 Gb / 2 Gb / 4 Gb / 8 Gb (JESD79-3C).
Fly-by command/address/control routing on DIMMs (instead of T-branch of DDR2) for improved signal integrity above 800 MT/s.
topology_summary: Source-synchronous parallel memory bus. A single DDR3 controller (master) drives CK/CK#, CKE, CS#, ODT, RAS#/CAS#/WE#, BA[2:0], A[15:0], DM, RESET# to one or more DDR3 SDRAM devices (slaves). DQ, DQS/DQS#, DM are bidirectional between controller and SDRAM. DIMMs use fly-by routing for command/address/control with per-DRAM termination at end-of-line; the controller compensates flight-time skew using the Write Leveling feature.

revision_history.description: Initial DDR3 SDRAM Standard release by JEDEC JC-42.3.
Added MR3 Multi Purpose Register, expanded speed bins, write leveling clarifications.
Current revision — ASR / SRT extensions, ODT timing refinements, 4 Gb density support, x16 ballout updates; differences from JESD79-3B documented in Annex A.

use_cases: Main memory in personal computers, servers, and workstations (UDIMM, SO-DIMM, RDIMM, LRDIMM modules).
Embedded and industrial systems with high memory bandwidth requirements.
Graphics and video buffers (though GDDR3 / GDDR5 dominate dedicated GPU memory).
Set-top boxes, IPTV, gaming consoles of the late-2000s / early-2010s generation.
FPGA-attached external memory via DDR3 PHY hard or soft IP.
overview: The DDR3 SDRAM is a high-speed dynamic random-access memory internally configured as an eight-bank DRAM. DDR3 SDRAM uses an 8n-prefetch architecture to achieve high-speed operation. The 8n-prefetch is combined with an interface designed to transfer two data words per clock cycle at the I/O pins. Read and write operations are burst oriented, start at a selected location, and continue for a burst length of eight (BL8) or a 'chopped' burst of four (BC4) in a programmed sequence. Operation begins with the registration of an Active command, which is then followed by a Read or Write command. The address bits registered coincident with the Active command select the bank and row to be activated; the address bits registered coincident with the Read or Write command select the starting column for the burst, determine if auto-precharge is to be performed (via A10), and select BC4 or BL8 mode 'on-the-fly' (via A12) if enabled in the mode register. Prior to normal operation, the DDR3 SDRAM must be powered up and initialized through a defined RESET# / CKE / MRS / ZQCL sequence.
